text: Penalty Clause 4.1 — Late Delivery: If the carrier fails to deliver goods by the agreed delivery date and time, the carrier shall be liable for a penalty of 0.5% of the total freight rate per hour of delay, up to a maximum of 15% of the total freight value. Delays caused by force majeure events, severe weather conditions, or documented road closures are exempt from this penalty clause provided the carrier notifies the shipper within 2 hours of the delay event.

Penalty Clause 4.2 — Overbilling: Any invoice submitted by the carrier that exceeds the agreed freight rate by more than 5% without prior written authorization from the shipper shall be considered an overbilling event. The shipper reserves the right to reject such invoices and demand a corrected invoice within 48 hours. Repeated overbilling events (more than 2 in any 6-month period) may result in immediate contract termination.

Penalty Clause 4.3 — Cargo Damage: In the event that goods are damaged during transit due to improper securing, temperature deviation, or carrier negligence, the carrier shall be liable for the full replacement value of the damaged goods, less any applicable insurance deductible. Claims must be filed within 5 business days of delivery. Supporting documentation including photographs and delivery receipts must accompany all damage claims.

Rate Schedule 2.1 — Standard Freight Rates: Base rates are calculated per kilometre per tonne of cargo. The base rate for dry van transport within the EU is EUR 1.20 per km per tonne. Reefer transport incurs a 25% surcharge on the base rate. Hazardous materials transport requires a 40% surcharge and advance notification of 48 hours. Fuel adjustment clauses apply quarterly based on the EU diesel index.

Rate Schedule 2.2 — Agreed Rate Binding: Once a freight rate has been agreed upon and confirmed in writing (email or ERP system confirmation), the rate is binding for the duration of that specific shipment. Carriers may not unilaterally increase rates after load acceptance. Any rate disputes must be raised before the load departs the origin facility. Post-delivery rate disputes are not accepted unless evidence of manifest billing error is provided.

Payment Terms 5.1 — Invoice Settlement: Invoices must be submitted within 7 calendar days of delivery confirmation. Standard payment terms are NET 30 from invoice receipt. Early payment discounts of 2% are available for invoices settled within 10 business days. Late payment by the shipper incurs interest at 8% per annum on the outstanding balance, calculated daily. Invoices submitted more than 30 days after delivery will not be processed.

Terms 6.1 — Dispute Resolution: Any billing dispute must be raised in writing within 14 calendar days of invoice receipt. The disputing party must provide specific line-item objections supported by documentation. Disputes will be reviewed by a joint committee within 21 business days. If no resolution is reached, the matter will be referred to binding arbitration under the ICC Rules. Neither party may withhold undisputed portions of an invoice pending resolution of disputed items.

Fuel Surcharge Disputes: Fuel surcharges are calculated weekly based on the published EU diesel index. Surcharges are capped at 30% of the base freight rate. Any fuel surcharge that exceeds the capped rate will be treated as an overbilling event subject to the penalties described in Clause 4.2. Carriers must provide documentation of the applicable fuel index date used to calculate the surcharge in all invoices.

Compliance Penalty 7.1 — Documentation Failure: Failure to provide complete delivery documentation (signed POD, CMR waybill, temperature logs for reefer loads) within 48 hours of delivery will result in a EUR 150 administrative penalty per missing document. Payment of such penalties will be deducted from the carrier's outstanding invoice. Repeated documentation failures may result in suspension from the carrier network.

Weight and Measurement 8.1: All weights are to be measured at origin using certified scales. The shipper's declared weight is binding unless the carrier provides a certified counter-measurement at origin. Overweight loads that exceed legal limits are the sole responsibility of the carrier. The shipper shall not be liable for fines, permits, or delays arising from overweight violations. Weight discrepancies of more than 2% between declared and actual weight may trigger invoice adjustment.
